subject: Genetics
title: Sickle Cell Disease
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Sickle Cell Disease.

hook.text: One amino acid swap—glutamate to valine—warps red blood cells into crescents that clog vessels.

buildup.text: Sickle cells are rigid and sticky. They block small vessels, causing pain crises, organ damage, and shortened life.

discovery.text: SCD was the first disease linked to a molecular defect—by Linus Pauling in 1949. Molecular medicine started here.

twist.text: In 2023, the FDA approved Casgevy—the first CRISPR gene therapy—for sickle cell. Gene editing met its moment.

climax.text: From the first molecular disease to the first CRISPR cure. Sickle cell bookends the history of genetics.

punchline.text: One amino acid. One disease. One CRISPR cure.

quiz.question: What was the first disease linked to a molecular defect?
